messages:
support_jess: Hey team — we just got a support ticket (#12345) from a customer who cannot access their project console after our SSO change. They sign in successfully but see `403 Permission Denied` as soon as they click into the project. They report the UI shows: `403 — missing project:viewer`. Ticket has screenshots and the Okta app logs.

maya-ss: thanks Jess. can you paste the customer org id + one affected user email? also did they migrate from SCIM or did they just flip the SSO app config?

support_jess: Org: org_acme_42, user: elena@acme.com. They said they did a recent IdP change last night (Okta) — renamed a claim from `groups` -> `roles` to match a new internal schema. They did not touch SCIM group sync. Quote from their Okta admin: "we changed the group-claim to `roles` for other apps".

samir: interesting — our console RBAC currently tries to map `groups` claim from the ID token to assert project access (we also accept SCIM group links). If Okta is sending `roles` instead, the token might contain the role name rather than the expected group attribute. can you get a sample id_token (redact) or a decoded payload from the affected user?

support_jess: customer pasted a redacted JWT payload into the ticket. here's the sanitized payload they provided:

```
{
  "sub": "00u123...",
  "email": "elena@acme.com",
  "preferred_username": "elena",
  "roles": ["project-viewer"],
  "iat": 1700000000,
  "exp": 1700003600
}
```

support_jess: note: there is a `roles` array but NO `groups` claim. that matches their note about renaming.

alex_devops: that would explain 403 if our mapping only looks at `groups`. can you reproduce the API call that fails? customer gave this curl output:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <id_token>" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects/org_acme_42/projects
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "missing required role or group: project-viewer",
  "code": 403
}
```

samir: yep. short term workarounds:
- add the user to a mapped SCIM group that exists on our side (if they use SCIM)
- configure Okta to emit `groups` again (map `roles` -> `groups` in the Okta app)
- give the user a direct project-level role from the Console UI (Org admin required)

support_jess: customer asks for the safest immediate fix; they don't want org admin changes but can update Okta. they asked if we can accept `roles` claim as a fallback on our side.

samir: we can accept `roles` as a fallback, but that requires a small change in auth-service and a deploy. I can push a hotfix branch that treats `roles` like `groups` for token mapping, but need product approval because it slightly widens accepted claim semantics. @maya-ss can you help triage with product? also adding an audit note in the DB is important if we auto-interpret claims.

maya-ss: tagging @product-idp (not in thread) — quick question for product: are there any compliance concerns about accepting `roles` as an alternate claim for group-based RBAC? if not, we can fast-track a fallback.

alex_devops: in meantime, here's how the customer can check their Okta mapping: Admin Console > Applications > Redwood App > Sign On > Edit SAML / OIDC claim: set `groups` to `user.groups` or add a transform that copies `user.roles` -> `groups`. Okta docs: https://okta.help/transform-claims

support_jess: Customer tried the Okta change and re-auth'd — they still saw 403. I asked them to capture the new token; they posted it and the payload STILL had no `groups` claim but `roles` present. they said the Okta transform didn't persist because their org uses a template pipeline.

samir: let's collect a server-side trace. @alex_devops can you tail the auth-service logs for that org id and request id? look for lines with `auth:map:groups` and token validation. also run:

```
kubectl logs deploy/auth-service -n prod --since=1h | grep "org_acme_42" | tail -n 200
```

alex_devops: grabbing logs now. I see this in the trace:

```
INFO auth:validate token sub=00u123... org=org_acme_42
DEBUG auth:map:groups claim=groups found=false claim=roles found=true
WARN auth:map:fallback roles present but no groups mapping for org org_acme_42
ERROR auth:authorize user=elena@acme.com allowed=false reason=missing_group_project-viewer
```

alex_devops: so auth-service already logs the fallback detection but we explicitly deny unless there's an org-level mapping that tells us to accept `roles`. that mapping is controlled by the identity integration settings per-org.

support_jess: customer asked how they can get an org-level mapping toggled now — they are not org admins. is there a support-allowed escalation path?

samir: we can create a temporary org policy toggle for them (we have an internal support path) — it will be annotated and expire in 30 minutes. to do that I need the org id and an approval from @maya-ss.

maya-ss: I approve a one-off support toggle for org_acme_42 to accept `roles` as fallback for 30 minutes so they can re-auth and confirm. please add an audit note and contact the customer about the temporary nature.

oncall-bot: Incident note created — ID INC-2026-8734 — ephemeral policy applied to org_acme_42: accept_roles_fallback=true TTL=30m — actor=maya-ss

support_jess: applied the temporary toggle and asked customer to log out and sign in again. customer_elena: i logged out, signed in, and now i can access the project — no more 403. thank you! :tada:

support_jess: great — marking ticket as resolved for now. next steps:
- open product ticket to consider adding a configurable fallback that accepts `roles` -> `groups` at org-level (owner opt-in)
- add doc snippet to SSO guide about claim names and an Okta transform example
- follow-up with the customer to plan a permanent fix (either update Okta app or add SCIM group link)

samir: I opened GH issue redwood/auth#4572 with the implementation notes and a risk assessment. tagging @security for review of claim-interpretation.

support_jess: closing loop with customer and adding a KB article.

customer_elena: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. i left a thumbs-up in the ticket. :thumbsup:
